name: KERF

intro.problem: Background estimates that assume the discriminants factorize fail when they are correlated, and product-form or rigid parametric models of the joint background miss exactly that dependence, especially in sparse tails.
intro.value: A flexible kernel model of the joint background could capture the dependence that factorized estimates miss and attach an uncertainty to it, turning a known failure mode into a measured correction.
intro.approach: We model marginals and the joint background with kernel density and kernel regression, combine them with maximum-entropy constraints, compare kernel families head to head, and score every variant on closure rather than fit quality alone.
intro.goals: The outcome is a framework for comparing kernels on background closure with honest uncertainties, and a recommendation for which kernels remain robust where the data are sparse.

questions: Can a kernel model of the joint background recover dependence that a factorized estimate misses?
Which kernel families stay robust in sparse tails?
Does combining kernels with maximum-entropy constraints improve closure without overfitting?

timeline.label: MaxEnt background model specified: product of fitted marginals plus dependence rungs
First MaxEnt ladder run: product baseline, Gaussian copula, and mixture copula rungs
Second-generation MaxEnt planned; literature and novelty check
Kernel MaxEnt plan locked: kernel-selected dependence term, gated test plan, genealogy deck
Kernel models explored for the low-statistics barrel region
Formalized as its own project and named KERF
Gated tests: toy harness, structure check, blinded toy closure, held-out corners, signal injection

links.title: Applied in the barrel program
links.text: The barrel is the region where a factorized estimate is least trustworthy and statistics are thinnest. STAVE applies this joint-background model there and scores it against the shared barrel baseline.
